stories.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
stories.summary: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. stories.summary: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. stories.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

items.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
items.summary: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. items.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson.
